Trump said no prisoner swap was required, but later argued that his decision to suspend new sanctions helped prevent negotiations for Hubbard’s release from collapsing. Witkoff said the discussions with Putin were constructive. items.title: [phys.org] Full-scale wave test shows salt marshes can buffer coastal storms
items.content_html:
🌾 ✏️

Researchers moved 306 square meters of intact salt marsh into the Delta Flume, a large wave-testing facility in Delft, Netherlands, and exposed it to waves as high as 2 meters. After 21 hours, the marsh surface had eroded by an average of just 7 millimeters, while its vegetation suffered progressive damage. The study found that plants can reduce wave energy by more than 10%, and by as much as 50% on lower-energy coasts with waves up to 1 meter. Their effect declines as waves grow higher and vegetation is lost. Researchers say marshes could work alongside dikes and seawalls, not replace them. A Spanish coastal-engineering expert questioned how well the Dutch experiment applies to other coastlines, citing wave periods and mobile seabeds among other factors.

items.title: [scitechdaily.com] Stanford team revives bleached corals through brief clone contact
items.content_html:
🌾 ✏️

Stanford researchers report that bleached coral fragments fully recovered within seven weeks in laboratory tests after brief contact with healthy, genetically identical clones, according to a study published Oct. 14 in *Science Advances*. Contact lasting five days to a week was sometimes enough; bleached fragments kept a few millimeters away from healthy partners died. Microscopic channels in the corals’ tissues aligned, allowing beneficial algae to move between fragments within three days. Inside bleached fragments, algae populations doubled every four days during the second week. The method requires matching clones, limiting its use across reefs. The researchers plan to test other ways to deliver algae, including collecting it from healthy corals before heat waves.

The package installed a credential stealer and a backdoor that could collect cloud and AI service keys, private keys, browser data and other secrets. Ushakov said the proposals contained little useful material. Moscow continues to seek terms Kyiv rejects, including Russian control of all of Donetsk and a bar on Ukrainian NATO membership. A technical-level meeting is the next step, but no firm date or venue has been announced. The Kremlin said talks could begin after Nov. 10.

The nonbinding Oct. 19 referendum also asked about immigration and constitutional changes. Preliminary results showed majorities for eight of the other nine proposals.
